_readme: Commonplace database. Each entry: author, text, cite, and optionally show:false (kept in the database but never displayed, e.g. unconfirmed readings). The About page draws a random handful of the shorter entries on every visit. Add entries anywhere; order does not matter.

quotes.author: Thomas Nagel
quotes.text: There is no view from nowhere.

quotes.author: Francisco J. Varela
quotes.text: Our current notions about evolution and brain will be as distant to our grandchildren as this animistic cosmology is to us today.

quotes.author: Howard H. Pattee
quotes.text: Since we are free to make our own syntactic rules we are also free to interpret inherently simple events as messages in our own elaborate symbolic systems, and indeed this is what has generated all mythologies and probably several sciences.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Everywhere is nowhere. Food does no good and is not assimilated into the body if it leaves the stomach as soon as it is eaten; nothing hinders a cure so much as frequent change of medicine; no wound will heal when one salve is tried after another; a plant which is often moved can never grow strong.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Contented poverty is an honorable estate.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Some men shrink into dark corners, to such a degree that they see darkly by day.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Discuss the problem with Nature. She will tell you that she has created both day and night.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Easier to conquer a whole tribe than to conquer one man.

quotes.text: Unblest is he who thinks himself unblest.
quotes.cite: Letters to Lucilius, citing a poet

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Your good qualities should face inward.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: You can never straighten that which is crooked unless you use a ruler.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: The best ideas are common property.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: You do not know where death awaits you, so be ready for it everywhere.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Let your faults die before you die.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Even if sound minds were for sale, they would not find buyers. Depraved minds, however, are bought and sold every day.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Give over hoping that you can skim, by means of epitomes, the wisdom of distinguished men. Look into their wisdom as a whole; study it as a whole. They are working out a plan and weaving together, line upon line, a masterpiece, from which nothing can be taken away without injury to the whole. Examine the separate parts, if you like, provided you examine them as parts of the man himself.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: It is one thing to remember, another to know. Remembering is merely safeguarding something entrusted to memory; knowing, however, means making everything your own.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: The living voice is a great help.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Remedies don’t avail unless they remain in the system.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: We worship the sources of mighty rivers; we erect altars at places where great streams burst suddenly from hidden sources; we adore springs of hot water as divine, and consecrate certain pools because of their dark waters or their immeasurable depth. If you see a man who is unterrified in the midst of dangers, untouched by desires, happy in adversity, peaceful amid the storm, will not a feeling of reverence for him steal over you? A divine power has descended on that man. When a soul rises superior to other souls, when it is under control, when it passes through every experience as if it were of small account, when it smiles at our fears and at our prayers, it is stirred by a force from heaven. A thing like this cannot stand upright unless it be propped by the divine. Therefore, a greater part of it abides in that place from whence it came down to earth. Just as the rays of the sun do indeed touch the earth, but still abide at the source from which they were sent.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Man’s highest good is attained, if he has fulfilled the good for which nature designed him at birth. And what is it which reason demands of him? The easiest thing in the world: to live in accordance with his own nature. But this is turned into a hard task by the general madness of mankind; we push one another into vice. And how can a man be recalled to salvation, when he has no one to restrain him, and all mankind urge him on?

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Tell them what nature has made necessary and what superfluous; tell them how simple are the laws that she has laid down, how pleasant and unimpeded life is for those who follow these laws, but how bitter and perplexed it is for those who have put their trust in opinion rather than nature.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: I should deem your games of logic to be of some avail in relieving men’s burdens, if you could first show me what part of these burdens they will relieve. What among these games of yours banishes lust? Or controls it? Would that I could say that they were merely of no profit! They are positively harmful.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Frankness and simplicity beseem true goodness. When your time is so scant, what madness it is to learn superfluous things!

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Why will no man confess his faults? Because he is still in their grasp; only he who is awake can recount his dream.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: There is one point in which the sage has an advantage over the god; for a god is freed from terrors by the bounty of nature, the wise man by his own bounty. What a wonderful privilege, to have the weaknesses of a man and the serenity of a god!

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Our luxuries have condemned us to weakness; we have ceased to be able to do that which we have long declined to do.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Nothing could be dimmer than those torches, which enabled us, not to see amid the darkness, but to see the darkness.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Struggled both with mud and with dust on the same road, on the same day.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: There are certain emotions which no courage can avoid.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: We are weak, watery beings, standing in the midst of unrealities; therefore let us turn our minds to the things that are everlasting.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Every instant means the death of our previous condition.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: It makes a great difference whether a man is lengthening his life or his death. I shall rush out of a house that is crumbling and tottering.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: It is according to opinion that we suffer.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: That which was bitter to bear is pleasant to have borne.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: You know what a straight line is; but how does it benefit you if you do not know what is straight in this life of ours?

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: They know more about careful speaking than about careful living.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Wisdom’s best attribute is that it is not one of the gifts of fortune.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: No matter what trouble you mention, it has happened to many.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: If you set a high value on liberty, you must set a low value on everything else.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Eternity consists of opposites.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: That man is a weakling and a degenerate who struggles and maligns the order of the universe and would rather reform the gods than reform himself.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: The eagerness to learn should be regulated, so that it may not get in its own way.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Man’s speech is just like his life.
quotes.cite: Letters to Lucilius, citing a Greek proverb

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: Exactly as each individual man’s actions seem to speak, so people’s style of speaking often reproduces the general character of the time. The fault is sometimes due to the man, sometimes to his speech.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: No man’s ability has ever been approved without something being pardoned. If you seek to correct their errors, you destroy them.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.text: The soul is our king. If it be safe, the other functions remain on duty and serve with obedience; but the slightest lack of equilibrium in the soul causes them to waver along with it. And when the soul has yielded to pleasure, its functions and actions grow weak, and any undertaking comes from a nerveless and unsteady source.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: The forms of matter are finite, but matter is infinite. Form is a death sentence, matter is eternal life.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: There can be no power of god in the whole that is concerned for any one thing, though there may be a power concerned for the whole.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Man is an everlock in infinite withoutness.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Hazard has conditioned us to live in hazard.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: The Divine Solution is to govern by not governing in any sense that the governed can call being governed; that is, to constitute a situation in which the governed must govern themselves.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: If there had been a creator, his second act would have been to disappear.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Put dice on the table and leave the room; but make it seem possible to the players that you were never in the room.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Nothing is unique in its species, even a cosmos; though everything is unique in its own existing.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: We are designed to want: with nothing to want, we are like windmills in a world without wind.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: If a cosmos is infinite, it has no end. If it has no end, there can be no end it is serving. Its only end must lie in its means. It exists in order to exist.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: We want to be mastered, but we are masterless.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: God is caused by what it causes; is made necessary by what it necessitates; we cannot comprehend.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: God is eternally partially self-ignorant. If he knew all of himself, he could define himself. If he could define himself, he would be finite. But all he knows of himself is what he has created. What is created is his knowledge, what is potential is his mystery: mysterious in him and to him. All this applies equally to man.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Mystery, or unknowing, is energy. As soon as a mystery is explained, it ceases to be a source of mystery.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Pleasure is a product of death; not an escape from it.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Death is in us and outside us; beside us in every room, in every street, in every field, in every car, in every plane. Death is what we are not every moment that we are, and every moment that we are is the moment when the dice comes to rest. We are always playing Russian roulette.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Death itself dies. Every moment you live, it dies.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: God is a situation. Not a power, or a being, or an influence.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: Life is the price we pay for death, not the reverse. The worse our life, the more we pay; the better, the cheaper.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: The consciousness is a mirror reflecting a mirror; anything that enters this room can be endlessly reflected and its reflections reflected.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: In a happy world, all anxieties would be games. An anxiety is a lack that causes pain; a game is a lack that causes pleasure. Two different men in identical circumstances: what one may feel is an anxiety, while to the other it is a game.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: To be alone in an office, dozens of telephones all ringing at the same time. These anxieties should make us one. We all feel them. But we let them isolate us, as if the citizens of a country would defend it by each barricading himself in his own house.

quotes.author: John Fowles
quotes.text: There is no more sense in being unhappy at hazard in general than there is in hating hands because they can be cut off.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Divine things for the most part escape recognition because of unbelief.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Nature loves to hide.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Conceit is a holy disease; sight tells falsehoods.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Uncomprehending when having heard, they are like the deaf. The saying describes them: being present they are absent.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: The lord whose oracle is at Delphi neither speaks nor conceals, but gives a sign.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: For the waking there is one common world, but when asleep each person turns away to a private one.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: What we see when awake is death, what we see asleep is sleep.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Unless he hopes for the unhoped for, he will not find it, since it is not to be hunted out and is impassable.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Those who seek gold dig up much earth but find little.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: People are deceived about the knowledge of obvious things. For children who were killing lice deceived Homer by saying: “All we saw and caught we left behind, but all we neither saw nor caught we bring with us.”

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: An unapparent connection is stronger than an apparent one.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Upon those who step into the same rivers, different and different waters flow.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: We step into and we do not step into the same rivers. We are and we are not.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: You would not discover the limits of the soul although you traveled every road: so deep a logos does it have.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: The soul has a self-increasing logos.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: This kosmos, the same for all, none of gods nor humans made, but it was always and is and shall be: an ever-living fire, kindled in measures and extinguished in measures.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: All things are an exchange for fire and fire for all things, as goods for gold and gold for goods.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Fire is want and satiety.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Fire lives the death of earth and air lives the death of fire, water lives the death of air, earth that of water.
quotes.note: element order unconfirmed (question marks in the notebook)

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: For souls, to become water is to die; for water to become earth is to die; but from earth, water comes to be; from water, soul.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Dry soul, wisest and best.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: A man when drunk: his soul is moist.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Changing, it rests.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: Even the kykeon falls apart if it is not stirred.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: What is opposed brings together; the finest harmony is composed of things at variance, and everything comes to be in accordance with strife.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: They do not understand how, though at variance with itself, it agrees with itself. It is a backwards-turning attunement like that of bow and lyre.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: The road up and the road down are one and the same.

quotes.author: Heraclitus
quotes.text: The beginning and the end are common on the circumference of a circle.
